an4.158:1.1: There Ven. Sāriputta addressed the monks,
an4.158:1.3: “Yes, friend,” the monks responded to him.
an4.158:2.1: “Friends, any monk or nun who sees four qualities in him- or herself should come to the conclusion,
an4.158:2.3: This is called decline by the Blessed One.’
an4.158:2.5: An increase in passion, an increase in aversion, an increase in delusion, and one’s eye of discernment makes no headway in terms of deep possibilities & impossibilities.
an4.158:2.6: Any monk or nun who sees these four qualities in him- or herself should come to the conclusion,
an4.158:2.8: This is called decline by the Blessed One.’
an4.158:3.1: “Any monk or nun who sees four qualities in him- or herself should come to the conclusion,
an4.158:3.2: ‘I am not declining in skillful qualities.
an4.158:3.3: This is called non-decline by the Blessed One.’
an4.158:3.5: A reduction in passion, a reduction in aversion, a reduction in delusion, and one’s eye of discernment makes headway in terms of deep possibilities & impossibilities.
an4.158:3.6: Any monk or nun who sees these four qualities in him- or herself should come to the conclusion,
an4.158:3.7: ‘I am not declining in skillful qualities.
an4.158:3.8: This is called non-decline by the Blessed One.’”
